title: Homological Cascade Engine: chain-complex diffusion, Hodge residual scoring, and streaming POT thresholds (research prototype)
description:
Experimental Python research software for exploring topological signal representations and robust anomaly scoring on multichannel telemetry. It provides a real-valued 2-complex with d1 d2 = 0, matrix-exponential diffusion over the 1-Laplacian, a Hodge decomposition (exact, co-exact, harmonic), median/MAD telemetry scoring, and static and non-stationary Peaks-Over-Threshold (Generalized Pareto) thresholds.

v0.6.0 adds a classical, synthetic residual-energy scorer (src.quantum.topological_ao) and a robust per-channel calibrator (src.analog_calibration). The scorer centres and scales frames, removes the common-mode offset, applies a contractive diffusion operator, and flags frames whose co-exact energy exceeds a streaming POT bound. Its names are motivated by free-space QKD and adaptive-optics background, but it runs only on synthetic real-valued vectors: it is not a QKD system, not adaptive-optics hardware, gives no quantum-security guarantee, does not detect real eavesdroppers, and has no measured latency. A flag means only that a frame's residual energy is unusually large relative to calibration data.

All results are SYNTHETIC (generated test inputs). No evaluation on real telemetry has been performed. Python 3.10+, NumPy and SciPy. Tests run in CI with a 90% coverage gate. License: MIT.
